A single step or stage in the succession of natural descent; a rank or degree in genealogy, the members of a family from the same parents, considered as a single unit.
Descent in a line from a common progenitor; progeny; descending line of offspring or ascending line of parentage.

A legal procedure done before a judge, without a jury, as with an evidentiary hearing.
Some other substance, often a detergent or another surfactant, able to mix with both oil and water, used for cleaning.
Soft, fluffy immature feathers which grow on young birds. Used as insulating material in duvets, sleeping bags and jackets.
The collection or mass of such growths growing from the skin of humans and animals, and forming a covering for any part or the whole body.

Seemingly, apparently, on the surface; supposedly, according to representations or implications made by someone (especially when their motives are suspected by others).
